params.text:
The 4 Cs of food safety

The FSA sums up safe food handling in four simple principles known as the 4 Cs: Cleaning, Cooking, Chilling and avoiding Cross-contamination. Together they cover the main ways harmful bacteria are killed, kept out or stopped from spreading. Applying the 4 Cs consistently, every time food is handled, is the foundation of good practice in any kitchen.

Keeping food out of the danger zone

Cooking and chilling both come down to temperature control. Harmful bacteria multiply most quickly between 8C and 63C - this range is known as the danger zone. The aim of temperature control is to keep food either cold enough or hot enough to stay out of it.

  • Keep your fridge at 5C or below so chilled food stays safe.
  • Cook and reheat food to a core temperature of 75C to kill bacteria (reheat food only once).
  • Hold hot food being served at 63C or above.
  • Cool cooked food quickly - ideally within 90 minutes - then refrigerate it.

Use a clean, calibrated probe thermometer to check core temperatures rather than relying on guesswork.

params.alt: A care worker, beside the heading “The 4 Cs of food safety”. Key points: 5C or below; 75C; 63C or above.

params.question: Which of the following are among the FSA's 4 Cs of food safety? (Select all that apply)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Keeping hands, surfaces and equipment clean is one of the 4 Cs.
Correct. Chilling keeps perishable food cold to slow bacterial growth.
Correct. Avoiding cross-contamination stops bacteria spreading between foods.
This is not one of the 4 Cs. The four are Cleaning, Cooking, Chilling and Cross-contamination.

params.textField: Harmful bacteria multiply fastest in the danger zone between 8 and *63* degrees Celsius. Keep your fridge at *5* degrees or below. Cook and reheat food to a core temperature of *75* degrees. Aim to cool cooked food within *90* minutes before refrigerating it.

params.question: It is safe to reheat the same portion of cooked food several times as long as it looks hot.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Food should only be reheated once, and must reach a core temperature of 75C. Repeated cycles through the danger zone let bacteria multiply.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Food should only be reheated once, and must reach 75C right through. Repeated reheating and cooling increases the risk of food poisoning.
